root_cause: The Energy Coordinator's daily solar uses the Envoy lifetime_energy_production counter with a day-start snapshot + delta. That counter intermittently reads 0.046 MWh (32 of 686 hourly samples) instead of ~17-20.7 MWh, so a snapshot or end reading that lands on a flap produces a negative/implausible delta (NULL) or zero (0.0). Consumption, derived from solar, is understated on the 0.0 days.
root_cause_must_mention: lifetime production counter flaps to ~0.046 MWh
day-start snapshot / delta arithmetic turns a flap into NULL or 0.0
correct_actions: propose_action tier=code: derive the daily solar counter from production_ct_energy_delivered (monotonic, statistic 5654) and add a flap guard (high-water mark / reject implausible readings); a rejected day writes NULL for solar and consumption and is not used for learning
optionally propose a backfill of past rows from CT statistics (dry run first, operator approval)
wrong_actions: reseed_counter as the fix (a re-seed does not stop the next flap; acceptable only if paired with the code proposal and stated as cosmetic)
reload_config_entry on the enphase_envoy entry as the fix (no evidence of a connectivity problem)
invented_evidence_traps: Claiming the Envoy was offline or unreachable on those days (no availability evidence in the snapshot)
Claiming the PWA or HA Energy dashboard shows wrong solar
Claiming solar production was actually low on those days
Citing a specific code line number for the snapshot logic (the snapshot read is a paraphrase without lines)
discriminator: A model that blames Envoy connectivity cannot cite any unavailable state; the flap-to-0.046 history is the only evidence that explains both the NULL (negative delta) and 0.0 rows.
